shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.note: Shortcuts are off while you type in an input field.

verdict.down_text: chronyd is not running – devices on the LAN are not getting time right now.
verdict.island_text: No time source reachable – the clock is free-running
verdict.syncing_text: chrony is still looking for a reliable source
verdict.good_text: The clock is synchronised and every part is running.

ntp.title: Time sources (NTP)
ntp.description: Where this server itself gets its time from.

lan.title: Time server for the LAN
lan.description: Who may ask this server and how it answers.

nts.title: NTS (Network Time Security)
nts.description: Cryptographically secured time – as a client and optionally as a server.

dns.title: DNS for ntp-gui
dns.description: Which DNS servers ntp-gui itself uses to resolve the names of its time sources – against loops when the LAN DNS rewrites time server names to ntp-gui.

gps.title: GPS / GNSS
gps.description: A GPS receiver as a reference clock of its own (stratum 0).

ptp.title: PTP (IEEE 1588)
ptp.description: Precision time over the network – needs suitable hardware.

language.label: Dashboard language
language.note: Applies to this browser only; without a choice German is used (English is in beta).
language.note_more: So far the navigation, the header, the status band on the overview and the sections here are translated – everything else, the ⓘ explanations and messages from the server are German for now.

settings.only_changed_none: Nothing in this area differs from the default.

badge.reset_title: Back to the default – takes effect when you save

preview.title: Preview: what saving writes
preview.unused: not used – stays as it is
preview.truncated: Shortened – the difference is very long.
preview.none: chrony.conf and ptp4l.conf stay as they are – the change only affects the dashboard.

settings.leave: The settings have unsaved changes. Leave anyway? The changes will be lost.

help.german_only: The explanations on this page are only available in German for now. Translations are welcome – see CONTRIBUTING.md.

api.title: API & automation
api.intro: For monitoring, scripts and Home Assistant. Once a password is set you need an API key (Settings → Dashboard → API keys); only /healthz is always open.
api.status: Overall state as JSON (the same data as the dashboard)
api.healthz: Short liveness check for containers and load balancers

clients.name_input: Own name for {address} (Enter saves, Esc cancels)
clients.ignore_42: Devices that ignore option 42 (Windows, Linux, macOS)

sources.steps_line: Measure → find the majority → pick the best → combine.

diagnose.intro: Log, events and diagnostic bundle for troubleshooting – nothing is uploaded automatically.

setup.title: Setup
setup.intro: Done in three minutes: five short steps, each optional. Only what you confirm with “Apply” is changed.
setup.intro_done: Setup is complete. You can revisit any step at any time.

lead.check: What the hardware check found. Every red item has exactly one fix to copy.
lead.sources: Where this server gets its time from. Templates add public NTS servers – your selection stays.
lead.gps: A GPS receiver is optional. Here is honestly what it brings.
lead.clients: This is how your devices ask this server for the time.
lead.notify: Optional: messages to your phone or Home Assistant. Without a channel nothing leaves the server.

setup.hidden: Setup complete – the assistant and checklist won't be shown again
setup.readonly: Read only: without admin rights (or with WEB_READONLY) nothing can be applied here.
setup.leave: There is a change in the assistant you have not applied yet. Leave the page anyway?
setup.holdover_confirm: A holdover test is running. Applying restarts chronyd and stops the test. Apply anyway?
setup.preview_none: The configuration files do not change.

sources.sub: NTS verifies the answers cryptographically – recommended. chrony itself checks whether the servers are reachable after applying.
sources.env: The list comes from the Compose file (NTP_SERVERS). Applying stores it in the dashboard, where it then takes precedence.
sources.keep: A template only adds – existing sources stay.

gps.optional: No receiver detected – that is fine, the time comes from the network.
gps.honest: Without PPS, GPS is a **fallback**: a USB GPS reaches 1–10 ms after calibration, good internet sources are usually more accurate. If the internet gets bad or fails – mobile, outage, island –, GPS takes over by itself.
gps.with_pps: With PPS the GPS is more accurate than any internet source and becomes the reference.
gps.question: Use GPS?
gps.no_receiver: Without a detected receiver GPS has nothing to read – check step 1 or the hardware page first.

clients.sub: Enter this server's address in your devices or your router. Most convenient: the router hands it out via DHCP option 42.
clients.router: Router (Pi-hole, OPNsense, UniFi, MikroTik …): Clients → set up clients →
clients.enforce: Devices with a built-in time server: enforce time server →
clients.smarthome: Smart home: guides for Home Assistant, Homepage, Glance and Uptime Kuma are in the repository under `docs/integrationen`.

notify.sub: Nothing is active by default. Create a channel and send a test message – or simply move on.
notify.no_right: Channels are visible with admin rights only.

hint.title: Review setup
hint.text: New in 1.6: a short assistant checks volume, permissions, GPS and time sources.
